title: Geospatial Mapping of Otitis Media (OM) and Social Determinants in Remote Northern Territory Communities
summary: NT Health proposes model-based disease-pattern analysis to guide ear-health services; existing GIS overlays and data coverage alone do not establish an AI benefit.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The proposed analysis combines a Bayesian hierarchical model and Power BI AI features to infer ear-disease patterns from health and social data in the Northern Territory. Existing mapping and seasonal DAX rules are conventional data-processing functions. The intended AI contribution is improved identification of areas needing services. The source does not specify the AI implementation fully or report resulting care improvements.
purpose: Use model-assisted disease-pattern analysis to guide targeted ear-health services.

ratings.reason: Model-assisted identification of high-risk areas is intended; the source does not establish a resulting planning or service improvement.
Improved hearing or care through model-guided targeting is intended, with no resulting patient outcome reported.
Reduced Indigenous health disparities are intended downstream effects of model-guided intervention.

ai_role.statement: The source identifies Bayesian hierarchical inference and planned Power BI AI features; map display, data integration, and fixed seasonal rules are not themselves the AI contribution.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 8: Geospatial Mapping of Otitis Media (OM) and Social Determinants in Remote Northern Territory Communities

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.

headline: Model-assisted ear-disease mapping aims to guide health services

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
